title: Fast Forward Awards 2026: HCP Sense, DeepGate, Myvox and LIOM
html:
Fast Forward Awards 2026: HCP Sense, DeepGate, Myvox and LIOM

HCP Sense, DeepGate, Myvox, and LIOM have won the Fast Forward Awards 2026, presented at electronica in Munich on 13 November. The four startups were recognised for technologies covering industrial condition monitoring, embedded AI, MEMS cooling and non-invasive health monitoring.

The awards concluded the tenth-anniversary edition of electronica Fast Forward, a startup programme organised in cooperation with Elektor. The winners were announced on the Smart Mobility Stage in Hall B4, with the results also confirmed in electronica’s official awards programme.

Fast Forward Awards 2026 winners

German startup HCP Sense received the electronica Fast Forward Award for its technology that uses mechanical bearings themselves as sensing elements. By measuring electrical impedance, the system can assess lubrication conditions and bearing loads during operation. The approach is intended to identify conditions that could cause premature wear or failure before significant mechanical damage develops.

British company DeepGate won the ST Innovation Award for its embedded AI development platform. The company’s compiler converts machine-learning models into optimised binaries for microcontrollers and provides benchmarking on physical hardware. In company-published benchmark results, DeepGate reports up to twice the inference speed and one-third of the RAM requirements of Google’s TensorFlow Lite Micro for selected workloads. Both companies were previously introduced by eeNews Europe in its Fast Forward Startup Spotlight coverage.

The Elektor Best Tech Award went to Swedish startup Myvox, which develops miniature airflow devices using piezoelectric microelectromechanical systems (MEMS). Its Airflow-in-a-Chip technology uses silicon-based actuators to move air without conventional rotating fans. The company is targeting compact electronic products where thermal management, noise and available space constrain cooling system design. Myvox is also developing MEMS devices for sound generation. Its technology was among those covered in the third startup spotlight.

Swiss company LIOM received the Elektor Future Impact Award for its work on non-invasive glucose monitoring. The company is developing a wrist-worn device that combines miniaturised photonics with Raman spectroscopy to obtain molecular information without penetrating the skin. Glucose is the initial target, with other biomarkers forming part of its longer-term development programme. The wearable remains under development and is not yet a commercially available glucose-monitoring product.

Prizes behind the Fast Forward Awards 2026

Each winner receives an international Elektor media package valued at €25,000, representing a combined €100,000 in media support. HCP Sense also receives an exhibition booth at electronica 2028, while DeepGate’s ST Innovation Award includes an opportunity to exhibit with STMicroelectronics at embedded world 2027.

The ceremony was hosted by Elektor’s Brian Tristam Williams and Udo Bormann. Award presenters included Katja Stolle of Messe München, Adriano Basile of STMicroelectronics, creator Max Imagination, and Elektor Editor-in-Chief Jens Nickel.
